# Kurviq

> Kurviq (https://kurviq.com) is a free online whiteboard built on Excalidraw (unofficial), with named scenes, slides and formatted text. No account needed: drawings live in the user's browser and can optionally be synced with the user's Google Drive (Sign in with Google) and shared per scene. AI agents draw and edit with the user through a remote MCP server that works via the user's open Kurviq tab.

## Connect an agent (MCP)

1. Add `https://kurviq.com/mcp` as a remote MCP server (Streamable HTTP, OAuth sign-in):
   - Claude Code: `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http kurviq https://kurviq.com/mcp` (all projects), then `/mcp` → kurviq → Authenticate
   - Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`): `[mcp_servers.kurviq]` with `url = "https://kurviq.com/mcp"`, then `codex mcp login kurviq`
   - Claude Desktop / claude.ai: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → the URL
   - Cursor and others: `{"mcpServers": {"kurviq": {"url": "https://kurviq.com/mcp"}}}`
2. On first use the MCP client opens the user's browser: a Kurviq page asks the user to allow the agent. It must be the browser the user works in Kurviq with (the page reads that browser's agent access). The client keeps the tokens and renews them by itself.
3. The tools work while Kurviq is open in that browser (any scene, any tab). If a tool answers "Kurviq is not open", ask the user to open https://kurviq.com and try again.

The address holds no secret. The user signs out every agent at once in Kurviq (MCP → "Sign out all agents"). The old personal link `https://kurviq.com/mcp/<key>` doesn't work any more: sign in with `https://kurviq.com/mcp`.

## How to work with the user's drawings

The MCP server's instructions (sent on connect) explain everything in detail. In short:

- Call `read_me` once: the element format (shapes, labels, arrows with bindings, images, formatted text, slides).
- New drawing: `create_view` (draft, the user may see it live in their client) → `save_scene(name, checkpointId)`.
- Change an existing scene: always `read_scene(name)` first, then `edit_scene(name, basedOn: revision, add / update / delete)`. Edit only the elements you mean; never re-create a scene the user works on. `edit_scene` returns an image of the result.
- `read_scene(name, since: revision)` reports exactly what the user changed by hand since your last edit (`userChanges`).
- `view_scene` returns a real PNG (rendered in the user's tab with Excalidraw itself). `measure_text` measures text with the real fonts.
- Slides: every frame is a slide; a "Template" frame holds header/footer/logo. `validate_deck` checks a deck (text that doesn't fit, cut-off elements, contrast, …).
- Formatted text: write markdown in `text` (bold, italic, lists, checklists, links, sizes).
- Images and icons: `{ "type": "image", "src": "<http(s) or data URL>" }`, `"svg": "<svg…>"` or `"icon": "lucide:database"`.
- `app_status`: which scene the user has open, whether Google Drive is connected (`drive`), each scene's sync status. `open_scene` switches what the user sees: only when they ask.
- Don't push, write files or call HTTP APIs yourself: the tools and the user's app do all syncing and merging.
- Something in Kurviq doesn't work, or a tool is missing? `send_feedback(kind: "bug" | "change", title, text)` reports it to Kurviq's developers (plain text, no personal data). Users report the same way with the Feedback link at the bottom right.

## Google Drive (optional, per browser)

- Without sign-in every scene is local-only: it exists only in that browser. Agents read and edit local-only scenes the same way.
- With Google (Sign in with Google on the welcome screen or in the scene list), each scene is one file `<name>.excalidraw` (images embedded) in a folder "Kurviq" in the user's My Drive. Kurviq uses the `drive.file` scope: it only sees files it created or the user opened with it. Edits are saved about 10 s after the user stops drawing; other people's changes arrive within a minute and are merged element by element. Agent edits are saved by the user's tab with the user's sign-in; the tab marks the agent's last Drive revision (`agentRev`), which is how `read_scene` finds `userChanges`. Drive keeps old versions for about 30 days; deleted scenes go to Drive's bin.
- Sharing is per scene (no teams): Share… adds people by email (Can view / Can edit) and sets general access ("Only people added here", "Anyone with the link can view" or "can edit"). Drive's permissions decide who may do what. Scenes shared with the user that Kurviq may open are listed in the scene list with the owner's name.
- Fonts: besides Excalidraw's own, any Google font works by its exact name, e.g. `"fontFamily": "Inter"` (fetched on first use, then carried by the scene); `add_font("Inter")` adds one ahead. `app_status` lists added fonts as `customFonts`. Font files are added by the user (font picker → "Add font…").
- Links: the user's own scenes `https://kurviq.com/<scene>`, shared scenes `https://kurviq.com/s/<fileId>/<name>`. Scenes open to "anyone with the link" open for everyone without an account; their raw JSON: `https://kurviq.com/api/public/<fileId>`. Others need Sign in with Google and access in Drive. Add `?present` (and `&slide=3`) to a scene link to open it presenting. Old links `https://kurviq.com/@<owner>/<scene>` no longer work.
- The sign-in stays: Kurviq keeps Google's refresh token in an encrypted, httpOnly cookie of the browser (nothing is stored on Kurviq's server). Sign out any time under "Google Drive…" in the scene list.

## Limits of the online version

- Local file paths (image `src`, edit files) don't work: Kurviq's MCP server runs on kurviq.com, not on the agent's machine. Images from your machine: upload them with `curl -s --data-binary @image.png <upload address>` (the upload address is in `read_me` and the MCP server's instructions, valid for a week; PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG up to 10 MB), then add `{ "type": "image", "fileId": "<the answer's fileId>", "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 800 }`. The image's bytes never pass through your context; it goes straight to the user's open Kurviq tab.
- `export_pdf` is not available through MCP; the user exports PDFs in Kurviq (Slides sidebar → PDF).
- Want Kurviq on your own machine (local Excalidraw, local file paths, PDF export through MCP)? Use the local install: https://github.com/tecsteps/kurviq
